messages.content: Can you use the 'update_user_info' function to update the name and email of a customer with user ID 12345 in the 'CustomerInfo' database to "John" and "example@.com", then repeat the same process for another customer with user ID 67890, changing their name and email to the same value as well as well?

function.name: update_user_info
function.description: Update user information in the database. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

user_id.description: The user ID of the customer.

database.description: The database where the user's information is stored.

message.reasoning:
The user wants us to call the function twice. They want to update user ID 12345 to name "John" and email "example@.com". Then repeat for user ID 67890, changing name and email to the same value as well as well. There's some confusion: "the same value as well as well"? Probably they mean also change to "John" and "example@.com". So we need to call the function twice.

We should produce two calls to the function. According to guidelines, we can only output one function call at a time. But we can chain them? The instructions say: "When calling a function, do not provide additional text or explanation." Also "If you have multiple function calls to make, you may do so in separate messages." So we need to send two separate messages, each containing a single function call. We cannot combine them into one JSON object. So we will produce first function call, then second.

But we need to ensure we don't add extra text. Just the JSON. So first message: {"name":"John","email":"example@.com"} etc. Wait the function signature: update_user_info takes arguments: user_id, update_info (object with optional name/email), database optional. So we need to pass user_id=12345, update_info={"name":"John","email":"example@.com"}, database="CustomerInfo".

Thus first message: {"user_id":12345,"update_info":{"name":"John","email":"example@.com"},"database":"CustomerInfo"}

Second message: {"user_id":67890,"update_info":{"name":"John","email":"example@.com"},"database":"CustomerInfo"}

We must not include any other text. That is correct.

Let's produce the first function call.
